I am a big fan of volleyball (all levels, but women’s NCAA is the main one I watch), and I think there’s a few interesting things to learn. For one thing, investment at the youth level is actually much higher for girls than boys, because all the higher level leagues that are successful are women’s leagues. This means that at the same age, girls generally have a higher skill level than boys. The difference in verticality and power then actually becomes an advantage for the women’s game, because for men the overwhelmingly dominant strategy is just to try to power the ball through, whereas women run all sorts of plays, motions and disguises in a game that is honestly pretty close to American football in it’s strategic complexity. I don’t see why this can’t happen in basketball as well.

The problem is players like Earl Monroe and Dave Bing getting automatically selected for the NBA 75 team when Dame and Dwight were much better.
